'''George E. Collins''' (born on January 10, 1928 in [[Stuart, Iowa]] – and died on November 21, 2017 in [[Madison, Wisconsin]])<ref name="obituary">{{Cite web |url=http://www.cs.wisc.edu/news/2017-12-11-memoriam-professor-emeritus-george-e-collins |title=In Memoriam: Professor Emeritus George E. Collins |access-date=2017-12-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180909133506/https://www.cs.wisc.edu/news/2017-12-11-memoriam-professor-emeritus-george-e-collins |archive-date=2018-09-09 |url-status=dead }}</ref> was an American [[mathematician]] and [[computer scientist]]. He is the inventor of [[Garbage collection (computer science)|garbage collection]] by [[reference counting]]{{ran|G60}}{{r|jones}}
and of the method of [[quantifier elimination]] by [[cylindrical algebraic decomposition]].{{ran|G75}}{{r|caviness}}

He received his PhD from [[Cornell University]] in 1955.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.genealogy.ams.org/id.php?id=75933|title = George Collins - the Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref> He worked at [[IBM]], the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] (1966–1986) [[Ohio State University]], [[Research Institute for Symbolic Computation|RISC-Linz]], [[University of Delaware]], and [[North Carolina State University]].<ref name="obituary" />

==Selected publications==
{{rma|G60|George E. Collins: A Method for Overlapping and Erasure of Lists, Commun. ACM, volume 3, number 12, 1960.}}

{{rma|G75|George E. Collins: Quantifier elimination for the elementary theory of real closed fields by cylindrical algebraic decomposition, Second GI Conf. Automata Theory and Formal Languages, Springer LNCS 33, 1975.}}
